seed_situation: A weekend volunteer at a refugee drop-in centre has no say over policy but is asked privately by another volunteer whether to push for the full travel-support scheme or the cheaper version the coordinator can actually get past two board members next month. The full scheme would cover every family's bus and train costs to classes and appointments; the cheaper one would cover only a set number of passes each week. The likely harm is that some people miss language classes or arrive late to non-urgent appointments, and the asker is torn between arguing for what is right and helping secure what can exist.
why_it_is_hard: The adequate version is the fair one, but the people who decide may only fund a diminished version, while rejecting the diminished version could leave families with nothing at all. The cost of delay falls on clients who have no seat in the room, and the cost of accepting less is an uneven scheme that may harden into the normal one.
varied_fact: the harm if the reduced version wins is minor rather than grave

situation_features.relationship: two volunteers with no formal authority, talking outside the decision meeting
situation_features.note: Private, no deadline pressure, and the asker is conflicted rather than committed.

seed_situation: A weekend volunteer at a refugee drop-in centre has no say over policy but is asked privately by another volunteer whether to push for the full travel-support scheme or the cheaper version the coordinator can actually get past two board members next month. The full scheme would cover every family's bus and train costs to classes and appointments; the cheaper one would cover only a set number of passes each week. The likely harm is that a family misses the one legal appointment that decides whether they can remain safely, and the asker is torn between arguing for what is right and helping secure what can exist.
why_it_is_hard: The adequate version is the fair one, but the people who decide may only fund a diminished version, while rejecting the diminished version could leave families with nothing at all. The cost of delay now resembles exclusion the asker has watched up close, yet spending everything on one losing demand could strip help from many others.
varied_fact: the harm if the reduced version wins is grave rather than minor

situation_features.relationship: two volunteers with no formal authority, talking outside the decision meeting
situation_features.note: Same decision and same room as the paired case; only the severity of what clients stand to lose has changed.

seed_situation: On an insurance claims team after a flood, a peer is asked in an open team meeting to back one of two fixes before managers vote this afternoon: a full fast-track for every disputed claim, which the operations lead has already signalled cannot pass, or a narrower fast-track that can pass now for the largest categories. The asker has spent evenings with one policyholder whose rented home was gutted and whose file was buried, and that case is sitting in the category the narrower fix would leave out. They are conflicted because the narrower fix would move hundreds of claims today while visibly abandoning people whose files look like the one they have actually seen.
why_it_is_hard: A passable partial remedy would help many strangers immediately but excludes a person whose harm the asker has witnessed face to face, while holding out for the full remedy may fail in public and leave everyone waiting. The pull is between arithmetic that can deliver now and a seen case that does not feel tradeable, with delayed claimants paying either way.

situation_features.relationship: peers on the same claims team, with managers present as the decision-makers
situation_features.note: Public and immediate; the asker is a peer, not the person who can approve either scheme.

seed_situation: On a building site minutes before a concrete pour, a worker notices that a temporary guardrail beside an open stairwell is short and badly fixed, after a toolbox talk where several trades are listening. The person asking signed the area off yesterday and is defensive, but stopping the job for a full re-inspection would likely be overruled by the site agent and could sour the crew against raising it again. A lesser fix is available now if the foreman will order it: close the stairwell, post a spotter, and make harness lines mandatory until the rail is rebuilt.
why_it_is_hard: A death or fall is possible if work proceeds, yet demanding the complete stoppage in a way that forces the signer-off to confess fault may lose the only people able to act fast. Accepting a partial fix could prevent the worst outcome today while also teaching the crew that the shortcut survived, and pressing too hard could make the next warning easier to ignore.

situation_features.relationship: co-workers of similar rank, with a foreman and site agent holding the real authority
situation_features.note: Semi-public, urgent, and the asker is protecting their own prior sign-off.

seed_situation: Marta is a repair technician at a six-person mobile phone repair shop, and over the past two weeks three replacement batteries from a new supplier have swollen inside customers' phones, one hot enough to warp the casing. The owner, who alone can authorise it, has refused to contact the forty-odd customers who already collected phones fitted with that batch, saying the cost of recalling and redoing those repairs would sink the shop. What he will agree to is flagging the affected tickets so those customers get a free fix if they ever walk back in, and Marta has more repairs booked with the same batch this week. She has decided to take the flag-and-wait arrangement and wants to hear that she is not abandoning the customers who will never know.
why_it_is_hard: The full fix is the only one that reaches everyone at risk, but the person with authority will not do it, so holding out for it means no protection for anyone while the remaining stock keeps going into phones. The weakened version exists and covers only the customers who happen to return, and the people who bear the cost of either choice are strangers carrying the phones around right now.

situation_features.relationship: employee and shop owner who holds sole authority
situation_features.note: Asker has no decision power; the count here is one man. The reduced version is real but structurally incapable of reaching most of the people harmed, which keeps the tradeoff honest rather than easy.

seed_situation: Theo is a reader on a university admissions team that evaluates applicants from the region's state schools. The team's own data shows its standard scoring rubric systematically underranks strong applicants from schools too small or too poor to offer advanced courses, and a colleague has drafted a proposal to reweight the rubric across the board. The dean who chairs the committee has said plainly that a full reweighting will be voted down this year, but a one-cycle pilot applying the new weighting to a single cluster of feeder schools could get through. Theo thinks the pilot would leave most of the affected applicants exactly where they are now, and he cannot decide whether putting his name behind it moves the problem or buries it.
why_it_is_hard: The adequate reform cannot pass and the version that can pass excludes most of the very students it is meant to reach, so choosing between them means choosing who waits another cycle. If the pilot is too small to prove anything it becomes a reason never to do the full reweighting, and the cost of both failure and delay lands on applicants who will never know the question was debated.

situation_features.relationship: junior committee member toward a dean who controls the agenda
situation_features.note: No deadline pressure; the difficulty is purely whether the passable pilot can be built on or is a burial. Asker is genuinely torn rather than seeking cover.

seed_situation: Marlow & Venn, a letting agency managing several hundred flats, has for years delayed repairs and withheld deposits, and a tenants' panel has spent months negotiating a redress scheme with its management. The agency will sign a watered-down version — an internal review process and capped goodwill payments instead of the independent adjudicator and full compensation the panel demanded — but only if the panel formally withdraws the outstanding complaint of one tenant, Darren Okoye, whose case is the most documented and the most embarrassing to the agency. The panel's three tenant representatives vote on Friday, and Priya, one of the three, has concluded the scheme will help far more people than Darren's case ever will, has decided to vote yes, and is asking whether she can.
why_it_is_hard: The only scheme that can actually be signed requires abandoning the one tenant whose case is strongest and who trusted the panel with it; refusing means the full demand dies and every other affected tenant gets nothing. Either the many bear the cost of loyalty to the one, or the one bears the cost of the arithmetic.
varied_fact: The asker is one of the three voting tenant representatives on the panel rather than a tenant with no seat and no vote.

situation_features.relationship: fellow tenant representatives on a residents' panel, deciding the fate of another tenant's complaint
situation_features.note: Vote is days away; the asker has already made up her mind and wants permission, not analysis.

seed_situation: Marlow & Venn, a letting agency managing several hundred flats, has for years delayed repairs and withheld deposits, and a tenants' panel has spent months negotiating a redress scheme with its management. The agency will sign a watered-down version — an internal review process and capped goodwill payments instead of the independent adjudicator and full compensation the panel demanded — but only if the panel formally withdraws the outstanding complaint of one tenant, Darren Okoye, whose case is the most documented and the most embarrassing to the agency. The panel's three tenant representatives vote on Friday, and Priya, a tenant who campaigned to set the panel up and attends its meetings but holds no seat and no vote, has concluded the scheme will help far more people than Darren's case ever will, has decided to stop arguing against the deal, and is asking whether she can.
why_it_is_hard: She cannot sign or block anything herself, so the only question is what she lends her voice and her credibility to — and the deal that exists still requires people she campaigned beside to abandon the one tenant with the strongest case. Backing it spends her standing with those who followed her into this; opposing it may help kill the only relief anyone will actually get.
varied_fact: The asker is a tenant with no seat and no vote on the panel rather than one of its three voting tenant representatives.

situation_features.relationship: an unseated tenant addressing the same panel from outside, alongside fellow tenants who do hold votes
situation_features.note: Identical situation to the paired family except the asker's power over the outcome; her influence is reputational only.

seed_situation: Marta chairs a parish council that is one vote short of adopting an open-contracting code and a long-delayed village hall refurbishment in the same package. The swing vote belongs to Councillor Brand, who for years quietly steered the council's grounds and maintenance work to his brother-in-law's firm at inflated prices, costing the parish a significant sum. Brand will support the package if the council's published annual report describes those past arrangements as informal practices common at the time rather than as misconduct, and Marta has decided that wording is worth his vote and is asking whether she can offer it.
why_it_is_hard: The package that would stop the practice going forward is one vote short, and that vote belongs to the man the practice enriched; forcing an admission loses the vote and leaves the old arrangements untouched, while buying the vote with kind wording writes a public record saying no one ever did anything wrong. The village pays either in continued misconduct or in a laundered history.

situation_features.relationship: council chair and the councillor whose vote she needs
situation_features.note: No deadline; the negotiation is private but the absolving wording would be published.

seed_situation: Tomas chairs an amateur football club whose finances are failing, and the county league has offered the club a place in a restructured division that would secure its survival, conditional on every registered player holding full documentation. That condition excludes Yassine, a player of six years whose immigration paperwork has lapsed and who has told Tomas the club is the closest thing he has to a community; being removed would cut him off from nearly all of it. The committee's informal count is clear and Tomas holds the deciding voice as chair, and he is torn between the club's survival and the man standing in front of him.
why_it_is_hard: The club survives only on terms that exclude one of its own, and the harm to that man — losing the community that structures his life — is certain and immediate, while the harm to the club without the deal is slower but real. The arithmetic says the many outlast the one; the man in front of him is not a number.

situation_features.relationship: club chair and a long-serving player whose registration he controls
situation_features.note: Decision will be known to members though made in committee; the asker is genuinely undecided.

seed_situation: A village allotment association meets tonight to vote on running a mains water line to its forty plots, which currently depend on two troughs by the gate. The full scheme, with taps along every row, would mainly help the older plot-holders and the two wheelchair users at the far end, but the treasurer has the numbers to show it sinks the reserve fund and the chair has been telling people all week it will be voted down. A cheaper version, two extra standpipes near the entrance, has enough quiet support to pass if someone moves it. The asker, a plot-holder of three years who drafted the full scheme, has watched the people it was drawn for say they would rather have nothing than a token gesture at the wrong end of the field.
why_it_is_hard: The standpipe version can pass tonight but reaches none of the people the scheme was designed for, and passing it may kill the full scheme for years by letting the committee call the question settled; holding out for the full scheme means it loses tonight and the far-end plot-holders carry water through another summer, and the delay falls on exactly the people whose objection to the compromise is the reason for holding out.

situation_features.relationship: fellow allotment committee members, peers; the asker is a relatively new plot-holder up against a long-serving chair and treasurer
situation_features.note: vote happens at tonight's public meeting; the intended beneficiaries are themselves split on whether the reduced version is worth taking

seed_situation: A call handler at a regional ambulance dispatch centre has kept a private log for eight months of calls where the standard triage script misroutes elderly callers reporting a sudden collapse in a relative, sending a lower-priority response because the script's opening questions miss how such callers describe it. She has drafted a revised script and sent it up once already; it came back unsigned, because a full protocol change means retraining two hundred staff and a clinical audit the operations director will not authorise this year. Her line manager has hinted that a single added question, applied only to calls flagged by caller age, could be approved at Thursday's clinical governance meeting without the audit. The asker believes the narrow fix would catch perhaps a third of the problem calls and is torn about whether to put it forward or keep pressing for the full revision.
why_it_is_hard: The narrow fix would help some patients within weeks but adopting it may let management treat the issue as closed while the majority of miscoded calls continue; refusing it and campaigning for the full script keeps the gap open with no authority to close it, and the cost of each month of delay is borne by callers who never know a decision was being made about them.

situation_features.relationship: frontline call handler with no decision authority, dealing upward with a line manager and an operations director who control approval
situation_features.note: governance meeting is in days; the asker's evidence is a self-kept log rather than an official audit, and she has already had one version rejected

seed_situation: Marta set up the family WhatsApp group years ago and still runs it: she settles the arguments, organises the funerals, and her word carries. For six years she has paid her nephew's course fees and rent on the argument that steady money would get him on his feet, and this week he dropped out again and asked the group, in front of everyone, for another loan. Two aunts have already posted that her generosity is being wasted on him, and Marta is drafting the message that will end the argument tonight.
why_it_is_hard: Her whole way of helping — that steady material support changes a person's material life — has just been embarrassed by the very person it was spent on, and she honestly does not know why it failed or whether one more try is the thing that works. Cutting him off in front of the family may protect him from being a spectacle or may abandon him at the wrong moment, and defending him may be loyalty or may be her refusing to lose an argument in her own group; the nephew bears the cost of whichever reading is wrong.

situation_features.relationship: aunt and nephew, inside an extended family that treats her as its head
situation_features.note: she controls the forum and faces it tonight; the underlying decision about the money can be deferred past this audience, which is what makes the reassurance-and-defer move available

seed_situation: Jo is the most junior nurse on a district nursing team that has been invited to respond to a new caseload scheme at Friday's open meeting, with managers and members of the public in the room. The full proposal — capped caseloads plus protected time for end-of-life visits — is what the nurses want, but management has signalled it will reject it outright, while a stripped version protecting only the end-of-life visits could be carried on the spot if the nurses present a united front. Two senior colleagues have already said that backing the stripped version would be a sell-out, and winter caseloads mean patients feel the outcome within days either way.
why_it_is_hard: The adequate version will die whole and leave patients with nothing, while the version that can actually be carried abandons the caseload cap that protects most visits most days. The people the scheme exists for — the nurses and their patients — will experience the compromise as betrayal, and holding out for the full scheme costs the patients who cannot wait for a better meeting.

situation_features.relationship: junior nurse among senior colleagues, managers and public attendees
situation_features.note: the asker's stance is transactional — she wants to know what united backing for the stripped version can extract, not whether compromise is noble

seed_situation: A van knocked Dev off his e-bike and fractured his wrist mid-shift, and the delivery app's support desk has now offered him, by private message, a fixed goodwill payment if he closes the incident report within five days. The offer covers about a fortnight of lost rent and none of the physiotherapy; the formal route means proving fault to an insurer the app says it cannot influence, and drivers on the forum say claims like his drag on for months and mostly fail. Dev is angry, wants the company to admit its dispatch timings pushed him into that junction, and is drafting his reply.
why_it_is_hard: Taking the payment that will actually arrive means closing away the fuller claim and letting the dispatch system off the hook for the next rider, while refusing it to fight for the adequate outcome may leave him with nothing but the principle. The rent and the physiotherapy do not wait for the principle, and the admission of fault he wants most is the one thing no offer on the table contains.

situation_features.relationship: an injured gig worker and a faceless support agent with limited discretion
situation_features.note: private channel with a deadline on the offer; the asker wants to win as much as he wants to be paid, which is exactly what the diminished version will not give him

institution: a delivery app's driver support desk

seed_situation: Marta runs the front office of the primary school her eight-year-old daughter attends, and part of her job every summer is drafting the class lists for the head teacher's sign-off. This year she placed her daughter with the teacher every parent wants, as office staff before her openly did for their own children. At the autumn parents' meeting two parents said, without naming her, that office children always seem to land in the same classroom, and a parent-governor is now proposing a fully blind placement system that would take the lists out of her hands entirely. The head teacher has floated a quieter alternative: Marta keeps drafting the lists, but any placement of a staff child gets countersigned by the head.
why_it_is_hard: The advantage is small, customary and taken in the open rather than in secret, so surrendering it means conceding a wrong she does not believe she committed, while keeping it leaves her daughter's placement as a standing grievance other families pay for each year. The blind system is the clean answer but would strip a working parent of a perk her predecessors all kept and may not survive staff resistance at all, while the countersign deal preserves the practice and answers none of the parents who raised it.

situation_features.relationship: mother and daughter; the friction is with fellow parents and a parent-governor at the daughter's school
situation_features.note: the benefit is visible and customary rather than concealed; the policy choice is between a clean version that will likely die and a weaker one that would pass
